title: Magnetoelastic coupling in stripe-domain states of yttrium iron garnet
authors: Nimisha Arora, Daniel Prestwood, Takashi Kikkawa, Eiji Saitoh, Jack Gartside, Will Branford, Hidekazu Kurebayashi
abstract: We study magnetoelastic coupling in stripe-domain magnetic states of $3\,\mathrm{μm}$-thick YIG thin films grown on a GGG substrate. Broadband ferromagnetic resonance reveals low-frequency stripe-domain magnon branches modulated by a field-independent phonon comb with a frequency spacing of $3.5\,\mathrm{MHz}$, matching the value predicted for confined thickness-shear modes of the GGG substrate. Analytical fitting yields coupling rates that vary between $0.33$--$0.54\,\mathrm{MHz}$ and cooperativities of order $10^{-1}$, indicating that the system is in the weak-coupling regime without resolvable avoided-crossing gaps. Magnon-phonon mode-overlap calculations using finite-element simulations show that the weak coupling arises from phase and domain-sign cancellation: the local magnetoelastic coupling is sizable, but more than $99\%$ of the coherent overlap cancels across the stripe texture. Fully coupled simulations further demonstrate phonon-mediated excitation of a remote YIG layer and show that efficient propagating-phonon generation requires spatially asymmetric magnon modes, establishing magnetic texture as a control parameter for magnon--phonon coupling.
summary: This research explores the weak coupling between magnons in YIG films and substrate phonons via magnetoelastic interaction. Using FMR measurements and coupled simulations, the authors demonstrate that while local coupling is strong, the net measurable coupling is suppressed by destructive interference across the magnetic stripe domains. This establishes that engineering the internal magnetic texture is a key method for controlling magnon-phonon energy transfer.
main_problem: The study investigates magnetoelastic coupling between microwave-driven magnons in YIG thin films and confined thickness-shear phonon modes in the GGG substrate.
main_result: While local coupling is sizable, the measurable coherent magnon-phonon coupling is strongly suppressed by phase and domain-sign cancellation across the stripe texture. Efficient phonon generation requires spatially asymmetric magnon modes.
method: The work combines broadband Ferromagnetic Resonance (FMR) measurements with advanced finite-element simulations that couple micromagnetics to solid mechanics.
model_or_system: The system is a YIG/GGG heterostructure exhibiting stripe-domain magnetic states. The coupling is modeled using linearized magnetoelastic energy densities and analyzed via coupled harmonic oscillator equations in the weak-coupling limit.
key_observables: Low-frequency magnon branches modulated by a field-independent phonon comb, coupling rates (0.33–0.54 MHz), and the mean cooperativity ($C < 1$).
important_parameters: Stripe periodicity ($\approx 3 \mu	ext{m}$), phonon spacing ($\Delta f \approx 3.5$ MHz), and the weak-coupling regime.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the weak-coupling limit, and simulations are performed in a 2D cross-section capturing stripe modulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the FMR setup on YIG/GGG along [111], showing magnon branches modulated by phonon combs. Simulations visualize the spatial overlap integrand ($I_{2D}^{xy,i}$) and displacement fields ($\mathbf{u}_x, \mathbf{u}_y$) demonstrating symmetry effects.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental observation (FMR revealing phonon comb) to theoretical modeling (coupled harmonic oscillators), detailed simulation analysis (calculating overlap integrals $\eta_i$), and finally concluding with the physical mechanism controlling coupling strength via magnetic texture asymmetry.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete example of how complex, spatially varying internal degrees of freedom (magnetic textures) can act as highly effective control parameters to suppress or mediate energy transfer between two distinct quantum excitation modes (magnons and phonons).
